Read the NAT_DATA layer catalogue

Source: R/natdata.R
read_natdata_metadata.Rd

Reads the catalogue of a NAT_DATA folder (ConsTech's shared national data), WTW_NAT_PREP_METADATA.csv, which lists its layers, one per row, with their folder, file name, output prefix and data type. The catalogue is returned with every one of its columns as they are, plus the full path of each layer's file, so it can be passed straight to extract_layers() with path_column = "file", after choosing the rows (layers) wanted.

Usage

read_natdata_metadata(
  natdata_dir,
  file = "WTW_NAT_PREP_METADATA.csv",
  active_only = TRUE
)

Arguments

natdata_dir

The NAT_DATA folder: a single path to an existing folder, such as a dated release (NAT_DATA_20261009). Where NAT_DATA lives is each tool's own setting; this function only reads from it.

file

The catalogue's file within natdata_dir, as a path relative to it. The default, "WTW_NAT_PREP_METADATA.csv", is NAT_DATA's catalogue, read by wtw-data-prep2 and the opportunity-screening-toolkit.

active_only

A single logical: TRUE (the default) keeps only the rows whose active column is TRUE, as wtw-data-prep2 and the toolkit do (rows where it is FALSE or empty are dropped), and needs an active column; FALSE keeps every row.

Value

A data frame with one row per layer (the active ones with active_only = TRUE) and the catalogue's columns, in its order, then file and subdir (character) unless the catalogue had them. Row names are 1 to the number of rows. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Reading: the catalogue is read as a UTF-8 CSV with utils::read.csv() (a byte order mark at the start is skipped), which guesses each column's type from its values: TRUE and FALSE become logical, numbers numeric, and the rest character, with empty cells as "" in character columns and NA in the others. Column names are kept as they are, except that spaces around them are removed (NAT_DATA's header has " file_name").

  • Rows: with active_only = TRUE, the rows where active is TRUE, in the catalogue's order.

  • Columns: every catalogue column is kept with its name, values and meaning. In NAT_DATA's catalogue, path is a layer's folder relative to natdata_dir (such as themes/species/eccc_ch), file_name its file, prefix the start of its output file names ("" for none), datatype the data type of its output files and type its role in a Where To Work project (include, theme, weight, ...). Two columns are added at the end, unless the catalogue already has a column of that name, which is then kept as it is:

    • file: the full path of the layer's file, file.path(natdata_dir, path, file_name) (without path when it is empty, and NA when file_name is empty);

    • subdir: a copy of path, the layer's folder, for the output folders extract_layers() writes to.

The catalogue's prefix, datatype and the added subdir are the columns extract_layers() reads for each layer; its type column is not extract_layers()'s format and is ignored there. The layers' files are not checked here; extract_layers() checks them before extracting.

See also

extract_layers() to extract the layers for an area of interest.

Other natdata: create_1km_grid(), natdata_template()

Examples

# A small NAT_DATA-like folder, with a catalogue of three active layers
# and one that is not
natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
layers <- read_natdata_metadata(natdata_dir)
layers[c("type", "file_name", "path", "prefix", "datatype", "subdir")]
#>     type    file_name           path prefix datatype         subdir
#> 1  theme features.rds themes/species     T_    INT1U themes/species
#> 2  theme    cover.tif themes/habitat     T_    INT2U themes/habitat
#> 3 weight    cover.tif themes/habitat     W_    FLT4S themes/habitat
basename(layers$file)
#> [1] "features.rds" "cover.tif"    "cover.tif"   

# Every row, active or not
nrow(read_natdata_metadata(natdata_dir, active_only = FALSE))
#> [1] 4

# Extract the layers for an AOI, with each layer's prefix, data type and
# folder (cover.tif is a GeoTIFF, which needs prioritizr)
if (requireNamespace("prioritizr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  template <- natdata_template(natdata_dir)
  aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
  aoi_raster <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")
  paths <- extract_layers(
    layers, aoi_raster, template,
    dir = file.path(tempdir(), "tifs"), path_column = "file"
  )
  basename(paths)
}
#> Dropped 1 row of
#> /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/natdata/themes/species/features.rds with
#> no values in the AOI: "sp_b".
#> [1] "T_sp_a.tif"  "T_cover.tif" "T_cover.tif" "W_cover.tif"
